pros: Is the best Fusion damage dealer currently in the game;
Has lots of different teammate options and performs well with all of them;
Signature weapon isn't necessary to perform alongside good teammates — standard 5-star is easily acceptable;
Has a really strong Dodge Counter combo, meaning she isn't affected by enemies being more aggressive provided the player can execute proper Perfect Dodging;
Her Outro only does damage, meaning she doesn't restrict the next character from quickswapping — this adds a lot to her damage ceiling.
cons: Has a rather bland playstyle only dependent on pressing Basic Attacks or occasionally executing Dodge Counters;

The overwhelming majority of her damage is loaded into the last two thirds of her rotation. In a meta where constant AoE output is important for one of the two hardest endgame modes, this significantly lowers her pull value;

Galbrena excels in the Mono Fusion team, but Changli is very competitive for her spot. Galbrena may be a redundant pull in this team if Changli is already owned, not because she isn't stronger, but because the difference is marginal (particularly if neither of them own their Signature weapon).

review.summary: Galbrena is a 5-star Fusion Pistol DPS who, despite what her weapon class would make you think, gets up close and personal with her targets to deal massive Cleave damage to them under her enhanced state called Demon Hypostasis. Accessing this state and optimizing its damage via Galbrena's numerous self-buffs included in her kit is the key to unleashing her full potential.

sections.heading: Review
paragraphs: Galbrena is a 5-star Fusion Pistol DPS who, despite what her weapon class would make you think, gets up close and personal with her targets to deal massive Cleave damage to them under her enhanced state called Demon Hypostasis. Accessing this state and optimizing its damage via Galbrena's numerous self-buffs included in her kit is the key to unleashing her full potential.

sections.heading: Key Mechanics
paragraphs: Galbrena's kit focuses around entering a stance called Demon Hypostasis. It allows her to cast massively enhanced attacks that deal the overwhelming majority of her damage at the cost of Forte points called Sinflame. They get converted 1 to 1 into Purging Flame which is then expended to cast her enhanced moves in Demon Hypostasis. As a result, the focus of her kit is generating her max of 100 Sinflame to then expend it after entering Demon Hypostasis, entered by casting her Enhanced Skill.
The amount of Sinflame currently generated is visible on her Forte bar, marked in blue outside of Demon Hypostasis. In Demon Hypostasis, only Purging Flame will be visible.

Via her Inherent Passives, Galbrena possesses Stamina recovery on a lot of her attacks, and a ramp-up DMG Amplify effect up to 20% which is easy to fully stack, as well as 20% ATK which will be up throughout most of her rotation. A lot of self-buffs make for a strong, self-sufficient kit.

Furthermore, she additionally possesses an extra Forte bar marked in red, and it stacks up to 40 points. It is called Afterflame, and it replenishes by casting Echo skills, at a rate of 8 points per. This increases the DMG Taken of enemies during Demon Hypostasis by up to 60% (1.5% per point).

The above is especially important because DMG Taken is a multiplier very rarely seen in character kits (mostly high Sequences like Cartethyia's and Phrolova's). On any character currently, in most cases it is rare enough to be considered a completely unique multiplier that buffs overall damage by whatever percentage is indicated. In other words, Galbrena's damage increases by up to 60% with multiple Echo skill casts on the team u can replace it by (in her best teams, this will typically not be maxed out and be left at 36% without Phrolova, 48% with Phrolova).
And for those who are curious: DMG Taken is the opposite of DMG Reduction observable in Tower of Adversity. They interact with one another directly and are considered the same damage multiplier.

sections.heading: Attacks outside of Demon Hypostasis
paragraphs: Outside of Demon Hypostasis, Galbrena will mostly want to execute Basic Attacks because they replenish her Forte gauge the fastest. As a result, we can exploit the following during her rotations:
Intro leads into Basic Attack 2;
Basic Attack 4 leads into Basic Attack 2;
Dodge Counter leads into Basic Attack 4 (situational).
Basic Attack 4 is a great Swap Cancel window if no Outro buffs are currently active on Galbrena.

Additionally, her Enhanced Skill has a very short animation as it is a very short slash which has a small amount of endlag. This endlag will be animation-cancelled on hit by her Ultimate to save a small amount of time.

Finally, her Ultimate increases the DMG multiplier of all attacks in Demon Hypostasis by 85% which means it is necessary to cast before entering Demon Hypostasis because this buff represents a massive damage boost. However, the 20% DMG Amplify from her Inherent skill should be fully stacked up before using it to maximize damage (simply doing Intro + Basic Attack + Enhanced Skill is sufficient!)

sections.heading: Attacks during Demon Hypostasis
paragraphs: During Demon Hypostasis, Galbrena only has her Basic Attack and Dodge Counter that she should worry about in order to fully expend her Forte gauge. There are 3 different properties to note here:
Ultimate leads into Basic Attack 2;
Basic Attack 5 leads into Basic Attack 3;
Dodge Counter leads into Basic Attack 4.

All of these properties are used in her rotation to skip out on the weak Basic Attack 1 and only focus on the much stronger Basic Attacks 3, 4 and 5 which have much higher damage values than the first two. Additionally, the Dodge Counter is really strong and for all intents and purposes replaces Basic Attack 3 as a better version, both in Forte consumption and in damage.

What this means is that Galbrena's full Dodge Counter combo is really strong and particularly important to execute whenever possible. If an enemy attack is incoming, make sure to Perfect Dodge it and execute her Dodge Counter combo to take Galbrena's damage to new heights!

Starting from max Forte, 2 Dodge Counter combos or 2 full Basic 3,4,5 combos can be executed (alongside a Basic 2 to start with). The final Basic 5 can and should be Swap Cancelled for optimal damage.

sections.heading: Unused parts of her kit
paragraphs: In practice, all of Galbrena's Mid-Air Attacks, her base Resonance Skill, her Hellstride attack, and all Heavy Attacks will go unused. They are not essential to her rotation and deal less damage than her Basic Attacks and Dodge Counters, so optimally Galbrena will not want to use them to optimize damage during her field time.

sections.heading: Meta Position & Conclusion
paragraphs: Galbrena is a very simple Basic Attack spam character, whose only real damage ceilings reside in her rotation outside of Demon Hypostasis (where her Forte gauge can be generated before Introing into her in certain teams, particularly those involving Lupa to nearly immediately go into Demon Hypostasis after Intro and save time) as well as her ability to execute strong Dodge Counters during Demon Hypostasis.

Beyond this, she has very little intricacies to her kit and as a result presents herself as a strong Fusion main damage dealer who can benefit from a wide variety of teammates, ranging from Brant/Mortefi + Lupa, to Phrolova + Shorekeeper, or even Mortefi + Shorekeeper/Verina for more F2P-accessible units. And the best part is that she can perform with all of these teammates. However, as the main damage dealer of all teams she is present in, she will definitely require a strong weapon to boot, ideally her Signature, but with strong teammates, she can function on Static Mist (the standard banner 5-star pistol) just fine.

In conclusion, Galbrena functions in a main damage dealer archetype that has been done several times in the past, but despite functioning in a classic role she is also very strong in her niche. Her only real weakness is multi-wave content found in Whimpering Wastes, due to the nature of her kit focusing around a strong burst damage window instead of constant damage output (which is generally favourable for multi-wave). With that being said, she can also function there given enough effort and a strong enough team, making her specialized against Boss encounters, yet still generally usable in AoE situations as well.

As the new best single-target Fusion damage dealer in the game, Galbrena cements herself a comfortable spot in the Wuthering Waves meta, using a variety of teammates, taking new and old characters alike to new heights.

When both effects are stacked, it even gives a small DEF Ignore boost to further increase this weapon's potential. Overall this is her best choice easily.

This makes it not face significant drop-offs compared to her Signature weapon, which isn't necessary to clear endgame contents thanks to Static Mist, provided Galbrena has good teammates to back her up.

Summon Echo that provides a small amount of damage and 20% Echo as well as 12% Fusion DMG Bonus when equipped in the main slot, being both of Galbrena's main damage types.

synergies.commentary: Galbrena's best Echo Damage buffers that provide multiple Echo Skill casts to fill up her Afterflame gauge, and amplify her Echo DMG via their Outros and other passives/weapon effects. Qiuyuan overall wins out by a slight margin as he sports buffs that apply more to Galbrena's 1/3 Heavy 2/3 Echo DMG split, whereas Lucilla really hones in on Echo DMG.

These 3 are the Mono Fusion team members for Galbrena, an archetype enabled by Lupa's insane buffs catered towards Fusion characters, particularly if the team is only comprised of them. Brant and Mortefi are great Outro buffers for Galbrena since they have 20% Fusion and 38 Heavy DMG Amplification respectively. Brant has higher personal damage which makes him perform at higher investments, but Mortefi is a totally fine alternative, and can even be considered for F2P Galbrena teams. Mono Fusion enabled by Lupa is one of Galbrena's best teams, particularly in Whimpering Wastes, and is definitely worth trying out!

Not Galbrena's best teammate choices, but in Galbrena teams Phrolova and Iuno respectively provide 25 and 50% Heavy DMG Amplification on their Outros, and they both deal very high personal damage. Phrolova is stronger than Iuno in the personal damage department and has an extra Echo Skill cast for Galbrena's Afterflame, so she tends to outclass Iuno for these reasons; however Iuno has a really easy rotation and extra healing if it is preferred. Rebecca is also a generalist Heavy DMG buffer with minimal upsides beyond that, but all of them can be worth considering if the above options are missing.

These 3 are the best generalist Supports in the game. Mornye has a special synergy with Galbrena and Lupa because she enables Galbrena to work in a Hypercarry team while still sporting Lupa's full Mono Fusion buffs which makes her the best choice if that's available. Otherwise, Shorekeeper is amazing thanks to her massive CRIT buffs and other generalist buffs, then Verina is the most accessible and still very strong option if neither are available.

example_teams.team_notes: Brant is only stronger than Mortefi at a minimum of S0R1 with endgame-level Echoes. Mortefi can outperform him at lower investments.
Phrolova is significantly stronger than Iuno here, making for a noticeable jump in power.
